newsitem.title: USA: CPAC buys IVAX unit's cleaning chemicals business.
newsitem.headline: CPAC buys IVAX unit's cleaning chemicals business.

text.p: CPAC Inc, a specialty chemical manufacturer, said Wednesday it has acquired certain assets of the commercial cleaning chemicals business of IVAX Industries Inc for $17 million in cash and assumption of certain liabilities.

The acquired business from the IVAX Corp unit had 1996 sales of about $25 million and includes the manufacturing and distribution of 177 chemical products for commercial and janitorial cleaning, it said.

CPAC said it plans to add the new acquisition to its newly formed Cleaning Technologies Group and operate it as a division of its Fuller Brush subsidiary in Great Bend, Kansas. Thomas Hendrickson, CPAC's chief executive officer, said his company had evaluated "many potential candidates" during the past 12 months and found the IVAX unit to be "the right strategic fit."
"As a division of Fuller Brush, the Cleaning Technologies Group will have the opportunity to expand its product line to include aerosols, brushes, and mops and brooms," he said.
Hendrickson said that the market for commercial cleaning chemicals is anticipated to reach $7 billion by the year 2000.
"Merging the two companies will establish CPAC as a significant player in this fastest growing segment of the cleaning industry," he said.

CPAC, which also owns five imaging chemical facilities in the U.S. and Europe, has over 250 registered trademarks for chemical and non-chemical products in the cleaning and personal care industry and imaging market.
In fiscal year ended March 31, 1997, the company had sales of $92.9 million and net profit of $7.5 million or $1.02 per share.
